decisions.reason: The product builds on the firm's existing knowledge of airport ground operations and electrical equipment, and its dedicated website page signals sufficient investment to support learning and improvement.
Apron connectivity aligns with the firm's expertise in electrical and communication equipment, allowing it to assimilate user feedback and refine the module.

Revenue calculation and billing software requires financial software knowledge far removed from the firm's electrical equipment base, so absorptive capacity is low and early results are difficult to interpret.
The product directly builds on the firm's core knowledge of apron electrical equipment, enabling it to effectively monitor performance data and enhance the software.
Resource management software uses operational data from apron equipment the firm understands well, supporting learning and incremental product improvement.
A safety alert service for air traffic controllers lies outside the firm's electrical equipment knowledge, so it cannot easily absorb feedback or develop the product further.
